stemEn: A newborn delivered with forceps is found to have an absent red reflex in one eye. Which diagnosis best explains this finding?
explanationAr: غياب الـ red reflex عند حديث الولادة يثير احتمال عتامة في المحور البصري؛ مفتاح المصدر اختار congenital cataract. تبقى الحاجة لمراجعة الصورة/الفحص الأصلي قبل اعتماد نهائي.
reasoningEn: The recalled key identifies congenital cataract as the cause of the absent unilateral red reflex.
clinicalPearl: Any abnormal or absent red reflex in an infant requires prompt ophthalmic assessment.

tts.text: A newborn delivered with forceps is found to have an absent red reflex in one eye. Which diagnosis best explains this finding? A. Congenital cataract. B. Retinal detachment. C. Retinoblastoma. D. Corneal birth trauma.

stemEn: An infant has strabismus with an abnormal unilateral red reflex. The recalled choices include CT brain-orbit imaging and TORCH screening. What was the recalled exam answer?
explanationAr: المصدر يذكر أن الإجابة المسترجعة قد تكون TORCH screening، لكنه يوضح بنفسه أن الأفضل سريريًا هو urgent ophthalmology referral مع comprehensive examination وقد يلزم EUA؛ كما ينبه لتجنب CT غير الضروري عند الاشتباه بـ retinoblastoma/RB1. لذلك السؤال محفوظ كـ conflicting.
reasoningEn: The source's recalled option does not match its own preferred clinical next step, so no verified answer is assigned.
clinicalPearl: Leukocoria is an urgent ophthalmic finding; retinoblastoma must be excluded promptly.
diagnosticSteps: Consider examination under anesthesia when required

tts.text: An infant has strabismus with an abnormal unilateral red reflex. The recalled choices are A. CT scan. B. TORCH screening.

stemEn: A 14-month-old boy is shown with unilateral leukocoria. The recalled choices are CT scan and TORCH screening. What was the recalled answer?
explanationAr: السؤال يعتمد على صورة leukocoria غير مرفوعة للمستودع. المصدر يقول إن B قد تكون الإجابة المسترجعة لكنه يؤكد أن الإجراء الأفضل هو urgent ophthalmology referral/EUA؛ لذلك لا يُعتمد للنشر حتى مراجعة الصورة والسياق.
reasoningEn: The recalled answer conflicts with the source's preferred clinical next step and the original image is required.
clinicalPearl: Unilateral leukocoria needs urgent specialist assessment.

stemEn: A 7-month-old infant presents with unilateral leukocoria. Which diagnosis is most likely?
explanationAr: بحسب مفتاح المصدر، unilateral leukocoria في هذا السيناريو تشير إلى retinoblastoma. يجب التعامل مع leukocoria كعلامة إنذار تستوجب تقييمًا عينيًا عاجلًا.
reasoningEn: The source key selects retinoblastoma for unilateral leukocoria in this infant.
clinicalPearl: Retinoblastoma is a critical diagnosis to exclude in any child with leukocoria.

stemEn: A child with an image suggestive of retinoblastoma is asked about a later associated malignancy. Which tumor is classically increased in risk?
explanationAr: المصدر يربط hereditary retinoblastoma/germline RB1 variants بزيادة خطر second primary tumors، ومن أبرزها osteosarcoma وsoft-tissue sarcomas.
reasoningEn: The recalled key identifies osteosarcoma as an important second malignancy associated with hereditary retinoblastoma.
clinicalPearl: Heritable RB1 disease carries lifelong risk of second primary malignancies.

stemEn: A 2-year-old has true strabismus on cover testing and a yellow-white pupillary reflex. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: اجتماع true strabismus مع leukocoria/white pupillary reflex من العلامات الكلاسيكية التي ترفع الاشتباه بقوة في retinoblastoma حسب المصدر.
reasoningEn: Leukocoria plus true strabismus is a classic presentation pattern of retinoblastoma.
incorrectOptionsAr: High myopia may contribute to ocular misalignment but does not explain a white pupillary reflex in this recalled scenario.
clinicalPearl: Strabismus can be the presenting complaint of retinoblastoma, especially when the red reflex is abnormal.

tts.text: A 2-year-old has true strabismus on cover testing and a yellow-white pupillary reflex. A. Retinoblastoma. B. Very high myopia.

stemEn: A 16-month-old appears cross-eyed, but the cover-uncover test shows no corrective movement and the corneal light reflex is centered symmetrically. What is the most likely diagnosis?
explanationAr: المظهر يوحي بالحول لكن Hirschberg/corneal light reflex مركزي والـ cover-uncover test طبيعي بلا refixation؛ هذه صورة pseudostrabismus حسب المصدر.
reasoningEn: Normal corneal light reflexes and a normal cover-uncover test support pseudostrabismus rather than true ocular misalignment.
clinicalPearl: Apparent esotropia with normal alignment tests is pseudostrabismus.
managementSteps: Routine visual follow-up as clinically indicated
